notes: Every training-compute threshold written into law, executive action or an official policy document, reviewed 2026-09. Whether a model crosses one is arithmetic on compute estimates and is not a legal finding.

records.applies_to: General-purpose AI models placed on the EU market
records.consequence: Presumption of systemic risk, bringing model evaluation, adversarial testing, incident reporting and cybersecurity obligations.
records.note: A rebuttable presumption rather than a hard line: a developer can argue its model does not carry systemic risk despite the compute, and the Commission can designate a model that falls below it.

records.instrument: SB 53, Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act
records.applies_to: Frontier developers training models above the threshold
records.consequence: Duty to publish a frontier AI framework and transparency report, and to report critical safety incidents to the state.
records.note: Counts the initial training run plus later fine-tuning and material modification, so it is a cumulative figure rather than a single-run one. Larger obligations attach above an annual revenue threshold as well.

records.consequence: Reporting of training runs, results of red-team testing and security measures.
records.note: The first compute threshold in any official instrument, revoked in January 2025. Included because it is still widely quoted as current, and because California later adopted the same number.

records.instrument: SB 1047, Safe and Secure Innovation for Frontier AI Models Act
records.applies_to: Developers of covered models above the threshold and above $100m training cost
records.consequence: Would have required a safety protocol, third-party audit and a shutdown capability.
records.note: Vetoed in September 2024. Its successor, SB 53, kept the compute threshold and dropped the audit and shutdown requirements.
